BUILD (reproduces the uploaded package byte-for-byte):
  Requirements: Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+, npm. Linux/macOS/Windows.
  Unzip the attached source, then in its folder:
    npm ci
    npm run build:firefox        # output: dist/firefox/
Third-party code comes only from npm (pdfjs-dist, preact) and is bundled by esbuild
(scripts/build.mjs). Nothing is downloaded or executed remotely.

LINTER WARNINGS come from bundled libraries:
- "Function constructor is eval": pdf.js's optional font-compilation path. Glimpse always
  calls pdf.js with isEvalSupported:false, so it is never used.
- innerHTML / dynamic import(): inside Preact and pdf.js. Glimpse's own innerHTML uses are
  static string literals.

PERMISSIONS
- <all_urls>: research PDFs live on any domain; we read the PDF being viewed, fetch cited
  papers' open-access PDFs, and call the Semantic Scholar/arXiv/Crossref/OpenAlex APIs.
- webRequest/webRequestBlocking: onHeadersReceived on top-level documents to recognise PDF
  responses and, only if the user chose "Always", redirect them to the bundled viewer
  (viewer.html, therefore web-accessible).
- webRequestFilterResponse: only for compiles.overleafusercontent.com output.pdf, to reuse
  the compiled PDF bytes Overleaf already downloads. The response passes through unmodified.
- scripting: injects content-main.js only into frames that contain a PDF viewer.
- pagefetch.js runs in the page's own context only on PDF-viewer pages: pdf.js cannot render
  inside Firefox's content-script compartment (Xray wrappers), so preview pages are rendered
  there and returned as blob URLs.

HOW TO TEST
1. Open https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762 and click the Glimpse button in the address bar
   (or the toolbar button -> "Open this PDF in Glimpse").
2. In Glimpse's viewer, hover a citation such as "[13]" and click "Preview".
3. The panel shows the cited paper's abstract; "Full PDF" renders it.
